critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py now ~7840 lines in a single module — the new CLASS EXTRAS block (lines 7447-7834) should be its own router module (e.g. routers/class_extras.py).

Delete authorization for class_announcements/class_agenda allows ANY guru/super_admin to delete regardless of class ownership. Consider gating by _assert_class_manage against the announcement's class_id so a guru from another class cannot delete.

Reply to a discussion only checks assert_class_view but NOT assert_class_unlocked — if a class later gets a password, cross-class members whose session is unlocked could still reply if endpoint is probed directly. Minor hardening.
SeatingIn: no validation that seats maps to actual class students; a malicious manager could persist arbitrary user ids as seat values. Add set-intersection with _class_students before saving.

class_announcements list sorts by `pinned` after Mongo sort by created_at desc — the second sort is stable-safe but it would be cleaner to sort server-side in a single Mongo pipeline (pinned desc, created_at desc).

In create_discussion the author's `kelas` ownership isn't explicitly verified beyond assert_class_view — siswa from a different kelas but who somehow passes assert_class_view (e.g. super role check) could post. Confirm assert_class_view correctly scopes siswa by `kelas` field.
